ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every shareholder, director, UBO, signatory, and principal business counterparty must be screened against the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Hong Kong's sanctions lists under the United Nations Sanctions Ordinance (Cap. 537), and the mainland Chinese and PRC government debarment and terrorism financing lists. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) include heads of state, senior government officials, judicial and military officers, SOE board members, and their immediate family and close associates. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any PEP, and all results must be recorded in writing with evidence of screening date, list version, and hit-resolution rationale. Ongoing transaction monitoring must cover Kickstarter, Stripe, PayPal, and trade-payment flows to ensure alignment with actual manufacturing invoices, customs declarations, and the stated tabletop dice casting business activity.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry e-Registry / Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Every Hong Kong company must have an English name; a Traditional Chinese name is optional. The English name must use Latin alphabets and must end with 'Limited' or the approved abbreviation 'Ltd.' The Chinese name, if adopted, must be in Traditional Chinese characters and may be identical or transliterated from the English name; no statutory Hanyu Pinyin phonetic transliteration is required for Hong Kong incorporation, but for mainland China bank and tax filings the English name will be recorded in Latin script and any Chinese entity name should follow the mainland convention of administrative division plus distinctive name plus industry plus organization form.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Companies Registry rejects a proposed name, the applicant must file a written appeal within 14 days of the rejection using ICRIS or by formal letter to the Registrar of Companies. The appeal must state the legal basis under Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), provide a revised name or a no-objection letter from the relevant regulator where the refusal arises from a sensitive token, and request re-search of the CRIS database. If the Registrar upholds the refusal, the applicant may, within 30 days of the final decision, apply for judicial review in the Court of First Instance under the High Court Ordinance; this administrative appeal route must be exhausted before judicial review is commenced.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is acceptable to the Companies Registry if it is a genuine physical Hong Kong address where legal process can be served, but it is materially rejected or disfavored by banks, Stripe, PayPal, and the Inland Revenue Department for an operating title involving manufacturing, inventory, and cross-border e-commerce. Without physical staff, stock, business records, and a substantive management presence in Hong Kong, the bank account and merchant accounts face denial, and the Inland Revenue Department may regard the Hong Kong entity as lacking commercial substance. Use a serviced office with private meeting rooms, displayed signage, a local company secretary, and maintained accounting records.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) confirm the registered office is a physical street address, not a P.O. Box; (2) ensure a person is present during business hours to accept service and tax notices; (3) maintain statutory books, Significant Controllers Register, financial records, and bank statements on site or at a designated agent in Hong Kong; (4) display the Business Registration Certificate at the registered office; (5) verify that mail and courier deliveries are actually received; and (6) ensure access for unannounced field visits from the Inland Revenue Department, Companies Registry, or police. Quantified risk for a low-risk handicraft RPG dice trading and light manufacturing coordination company is approximately 15 to 20 percent per year during the first three years, rising to over 40 percent if nil tax returns are filed, if SCR is incomplete, or if no substantial business records are found.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), Laws of Hong Kong; in particular sections 5, 67, 68, 112, 113, 114, 124, 474 and 475 and Schedule 1; Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) section 5; Factories and Industrial Undertakings Ordinance (Cap. 59) for manufacturing operations
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Registry, 13/F, Queensway Government Offices, 66 Queensway, Hong Kong SAR; e-Registry portal available at www.e-registry.com.hk
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NNC1 (Application for Incorporation of a Company Limited by Shares), together with the executed Articles of Association and Declaration of Compliance
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Under Cap. 622, a private company limited by shares may be incorporated with one or more shares of HKD 1.00 or any other denomination; there is no minimum paid-up share capital, no blocked escrow account and no capital verification certificate is required. Where a bank or counterparty requests capital evidence, the directors may pass a solvency statement or provide the share certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN JV LIMITED. At a duly convened first meeting of the Board of Directors of CN JV Limited, a private company limited by shares incorporated under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) of Hong Kong, held at the registered office of the Company, the following resolutions were proposed, seconded and unanimously passed. 1. Appointment of Directors and Company Secretary: RESOLVED that the first directors of the Company, being the persons whose names appear on Form NNC1, be and are hereby confirmed as the lawful directors of the Company, and that the person named as company secretary in the incorporation application be and is hereby appointed as the first Company Secretary of the Company, such appointments to take effect from the date of incorporation. 2. Adoption of Registered Office: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be fixed at the physical address stated in the incorporation application, being a premises within Hong Kong, and that the directors be and are hereby authorized to execute and deliver to the Companies Registry all consents, declarations and forms necessary to maintain such registered office and to receive service of process. 3. Share Capital Subscription and Allotment: RESOLVED that the subscriber shares be allotted in accordance with the Articles of Association, namely such number of ordinary shares of HKD 1.00 each as are set out in the statement of capital, credited as paid or credited as fully paid up as to cash; that the directors be and are hereby authorized to receive the subscription moneys, to issue share certificates under the common seal of the Company, and to enter the names of the subscribers in the register of members. The board notes that no statutory minimum paid-up capital exists under Cap. 622 and that no escrow account is required unless a particular bank imposes one. 4. Banking Authorization: RESOLVED that one or more bank accounts be opened with the licensed bank or banks selected by the directors; that the directors named in the bank mandate be and are hereby appointed as authorized signatories; that any two signatures be required for payments exceeding HKD 100,000 and any one signature for all other payments; that the bank be furnished with certified copies of these resolutions and the Certificate of Incorporation; and that the directors be authorized to sign the bank mandate and all ancillary documentation. 5. Statutory Records and Seal: RESOLVED that the Company adopt a common seal and establish the register of members, register of directors and company secretary, register of charges, register of significant controllers and minute book, and that the minutes of this meeting be signed by the chairperson. 6. General Authority: RESOLVED that the directors be and are hereby authorized to execute all documents, pay all incorporation fees, levies and regulatory charges, and take all steps necessary to complete the incorporation and licensing of the Company, including registration of the manufacturing premises under Cap. 59.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Clearance and Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR; Integrated Companies Registry Information System and e-Registry portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the proposed English and Chinese company names are not undesirable by conducting an electronic name search on the Companies Registry database. Because Hong Kong does not operate a formal name reservation system, the applicant should immediately submit Form NNC1 after clearance to prevent another applicant from registering a similar name. Complete every section of Form NNC1 on the e-Registry portal, attach the executed Articles of Association, subscriber consents, director consents and company secretary consents, and submit the declaration of compliance. Each subscriber signature must be witnessed by a qualified professional where physical execution is used, or submitted through the registered digital-signatory channel. Pay the composite government fee online. On approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and, through the one-stop service, the initial Business Registration Certificate.
required_dossiers: Copy of Hong Kong identity document or passport of each subscriber, director and secretary
Proof of residential address of each natural person officer
Consent to Act as Director and Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a Notice of Defects or Query, correct the stated defects within the specified period, usually 14 days, amend the digital form or execute supplementary documentation, and resubmit with an explanatory letter and any required reset fee. Do not abandon the application without a formal withdrawal because name priority may be lost; if the name conflict is accepted, choose a new name and file a fresh application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Profits Tax File Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Business Registration Office; one-stop integrated online filing channel with Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately upon receipt of the Certificate of Incorporation, secure a Business Registration Certificate under Cap. 310. If the application is not combined with the incorporation filing, file Form IRBR1 within one month of incorporation. State the registered address, principal business activity using ISIC code 3240, date of commencement of business and expected turnover. The Business Registration Office will issue the certificate and allocate a Business Registration Number; the Inland Revenue Department will subsequently open the profits tax file. The certificate must be renewed annually and displayed at each physical place of business in Hong Kong. Any change in the principal place of business or the addition of retail and online sales activity must be reported promptly.
required_dossiers: Board resolution confirming date of commencement of business
Business premises tenancy or ownership document
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, submit a written reply to the Business Registration Office within 21 days with the tenancy deed, a letter from the certified public accountant or company secretary confirming the business address, and a revised business description. If the query is based on incomplete information, pay the applicable late fee and file an amended IRBR1 rather than waiting for a reminder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment and Filing of Statutory Officers and Registered Office Adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry for statutory filings; board of directors for internal governance actions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Under Cap. 622, every private company must have at least one natural director and a company secretary; if the company has only one director, that director may not also be the company secretary. After the first board meeting approves the appointments, file Form ND2A with the Companies Registry within 14 days. The registered office must be a physical serviceable address in Hong Kong and cannot be a post office box. The company secretary must be an individual ordinarily resident in Hong Kong or a body corporate with a registered office in Hong Kong. Ensure the consent-to-act statements are retained in the statutory records. Place the company name in a prominent position at the registered office and at every place of business. The directors must also verify that the significant controllers register is ready for inspection in accordance with Cap. 622.
required_dossiers: Certified copies of identification of each officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry returns the form for correction, amend the officer particulars and refile within the specified time. If the filing is late, pay the prescribed late fee and submit a covering letter from the company secretary explaining the inadvertent delay; if the company has been threatened with prosecution, engage a solicitor to make a voluntary disclosure and mitigation submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Seal, Share Certificates and Statutory Records Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors and company secretary; Companies Registry as record custodian if public inspection arises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: At this stage the board must physically or electronically certify the issue of share certificates to the founding shareholders in accordance with the share capital subscription resolution. Adopt the common seal if required by the Articles, and direct the company secretary to maintain the register of members, register of directors and company secretary, register of charges, register of significant controllers, and minute book at the registered office. Each share certificate must be signed by at least one director and by the company secretary or by two directors where the seal is used. Record the allotment date, number of shares, consideration received and date of entry in the register of members. The company secretary should also prepare certified true copies of the Certificate of Incorporation, Business Registration Certificate and Articles for use in bank account opening, licensing and e-commerce merchant verification.
required_dossiers: Board resolution adopting seal and share certificates
Register of members and statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a defect in the statutory registers is discovered, remedy the omission by making a corrective entry, obtaining a board ratification resolution, and filing any required change-of-particulars form with the Companies Registry. If a share certificate is lost or defective, issue a replacement only after obtaining a board resolution, retaining a signed indemnity from the registered holder, and updating the register of members.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Mandate, Payment Rails and Merchant Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed bank under the Banking Ordinance (Cap. 155); Stripe, Kickstarter and PayPal for merchant account verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before the entity begins sales through Kickstarter Stripe and PayPal, open a corporate bank account with a licensed Hong Kong bank or licensed digital bank. Present the Certificate of Incorporation, Business Registration Certificate, certified articles, statutory registers, a certified board resolution appointing the bank signatories, and valid identification of each director and shareholder. The bank will assess source of funds, beneficial ownership and anti-money laundering risk; the standard expected rating is low risk but full know-your-client documentation is still required. After the bank account is opened, link the entity treasury account to the Kickstarter Stripe account and PayPal merchant account. Complete the merchant verification questionnaires using the exact legal entity name, registered office address, business website, product description as handmade sharp-edge epoxy resin liquid core RPG dice, and banking settlement instructions.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Articles of Association
Directors and shareholders passport or HKID copies
Proof of registered office and business address
Bank account opening and KYC forms
Stripe and PayPal merchant verification forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further information, respond within 14 days with a bank reference letter, certified financial projections and source-of-funds evidence. If the digital payment processor places the merchant account on hold, submit the signed board resolution, the certificate of incorporation, a compliance explanation and the product sales URL, and request escalation to a human underwriting officer.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Commissioner for Labour, Labour Department (Factories and Industrial Undertakings Ordinance); Fire Services Department; Environmental Protection Department; Buildings Department
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Factory Registration Certificate under the Factories and Industrial Undertakings Ordinance (Cap. 59); Dangerous Goods Licence under the Dangerous Goods Ordinance (Cap. 295) where flammable liquid thresholds are exceeded; Chemical Waste Producer Registration under the Waste Disposal Ordinance (Cap. 354)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Department, Hong Kong SAR (EPD)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not a Schedule 2 designated project under the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap. 499) at the contemplated scale; therefore a Full EIA Report and Environmental Permit are not mandatory. The operation is nevertheless subject to local environmental registration as a chemical waste producer and to effluent, air emission and dangerous goods compliance.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Process wastewater from resin mixing, curing, mold cleaning and floor scrubbing may be discharged to foul sewers only after pre-treatment and only if meeting the relevant Technical Memorandum limits under the Water Pollution Control Ordinance (Cap. 358), namely pH 6 to 10, temperature not exceeding 43 degrees Celsius, BOD5 not exceeding 100 mg/L, COD not exceeding 300 mg/L, total suspended solids not exceeding 50 mg/L and oil and grease not exceeding 30 mg/L; no discharge is permitted to storm drains unless separately licensed. Volatile organic compound emissions from acetone and epoxy resin work must be controlled by local exhaust ventilation so that the stack discharge concentration remains below 50 mgC/m3 and aggregate solvent consumption is documented to remain below 0.1 kg per hour per emission point. Chemical waste must be stored in leak-proof labeled containers within secondary containment of at least 110 percent of the largest container volume and removed only by a licensed chemical waste collector.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before commissioning the production line, obtain from the Fire Services Department a fire safety certificate for the industrial premises and verify that hydrants, extinguishers and emergency signage are adequate; if stored flammable liquids exceed 450 liters, obtain a Dangerous Goods Licence under Cap. 295. Provide a registered structural engineer letter confirming that floor loading is adequate for casting stations, liquid-core dice inventories and storage racks. Secure the Commissioner for Labour approval of the Factory Registration and machine-safety arrangements under Cap. 59, including guarding of mixers and curing equipment, local exhaust ventilation, personal protective equipment, first aid and emergency evacuation plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online filings are processed through the STA's Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) national online service platform maintained by the provincial tax services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture (CN_JV_LTD) is a PRC-resident enterprise formed under the PRC Foreign Investment Law and Company Law. After the company is incorporated at the local Administration for Market Regulation, it is granted a Uniform Social Credit Code, which automatically serves as the enterprise's tax identification number and VAT taxpayer identification number. The joint venture must complete consolidated tax registration through the Electronic Tax Bureau within 30 days of obtaining its business license, using the Uniform Social Credit Code as the TIN. For the Hong Kong non-resident shareholder, no standalone registration is required for the shareholder merely to hold equity; however, before the JV distributes dividends or makes any payment of China-source income to the Hong Kong parent, the Hong Kong parent must obtain a Non-resident Enterprise Tax Identification Code through the competent STA office at the place where the income arises, or be identified in the withholding registration. The Hong Kong parent must also furnish a Hong Kong resident certificate if it intends to claim treaty benefits under the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement. The JV itself is not a pass-through vehicle: it files corporate income tax and VAT under its own TIN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The JV is a PRC resident enterprise taxed on worldwide income under the Enterprise Income Tax Law at the standard 25% rate; all VAT obligations are borne by the JV. The Hong Kong SAR jurisdiction applies a territorial profits tax and has no VAT/GST, but Hong Kong treatment does not alter the PRC entity-level classification of the mainland JV.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC tax system does not provide check-the-box entity classification elections or hybrid-mismatch elections. The JV may apply for preferential EIT treatment (e.g., High and New Technology Enterprise, small low-profit enterprise) by administrative application, but such applications do not change entity-level taxpayer status. The HK shareholder may elect to apply the reduced 5% dividend withholding rate under the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement if it meets the beneficial ownership and 25%+ holding conditions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China under the PRC VAT Law and its implementing regulations
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All established enterprises must register for tax regardless of turnover; the Uniform Social Credit Code is the VAT TIN. The compulsory VAT general taxpayer registration threshold is annual taxable sales in excess of RMB 5,000,000. Below that threshold, the JV can remain a small-scale VAT taxpayer at a reduced collection rate, and monthly sales of RMB 100,000 (quarterly RMB 300,000) are exempt from VAT under current small-scale preferential policies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT invoices must be issued through the STA-managed digital electronic invoice platform (all-digital e-invoices), with real-time transmission to the taxation authority at the moment of issuance. The STA clears the invoice by validating the counterparty tax IDs, verifying the applicable rate, and applying a cryptographic anti-fraud digital stamp and unique invoice number. ERP/API machine-to-machine issuance is supported for high-volume sellers, while manual issuance on the Electronic Tax Bureau portal is permitted. Since export zero-rating is applied at the customs export declaration level, the e-invoice in an export transaction is normally not a zero-rated VAT invoice; the export price is declared as VAT-exempt for output VAT and the supported refund is recovered through the export tax rebate filing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: To claim the 0% export VAT rate for the manufactured epoxy-resin liquid-core RPG polyhedral dice, the JV must be the actual exporter, the goods must be physically declared to and cleared by PRC Customs and leave the PRC customs territory to an overseas destination (including Hong Kong SAR, which is outside the PRC customs territory for export purposes), and the JV must prove the sale, the real foreign buyer, the actual shipment, and the receipt of payment from outside China. The sale must be supported by a valid customs export declaration, an overseas transport document, a commercial invoice/contract, and foreign exchange receipt evidence. The export may be carried out under ordinary trade declarations or, for crowdfunded/online orders via Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal, under cross-border e-commerce export customs clearance; every parcel must have a customs declaration rather than being shipped only as untracked fulfilment. The qualifying production exporter then uses the export tax refund (exemption, set-off and refund) procedure to obtain refund of the input VAT embedded in manufacturing costs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export bill of entry / customs clearance form) bearing the export reference number, HS classification, quantity, unit value and actual export release date

Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (for direct-to-backer crowd shipments, the international express courier's shipping manifest and detailed delivery tracking proving departure from PRC customs and delivery to the overseas customer)
Commercial invoice, sales contract or order record (including Kickstarter backer ledger, Stripe/PayPal transaction statements) identifying the overseas buyer and the RPG polyhedral dice sets sold

Inward Remittance Certificate / bank foreign-exchange receipt (the Chinese export verification equivalent) and the Stripe/PayPal settlement-payout reports showing that export proceeds were actually collected and repatriated to China within the statutory period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA will cross-match the customs export declarations with the e-invoices, logistics tracking events, bank FX receipts and crowdfunding/payment-aggregator settlement data under the Golden Tax Phase IV data warehouse. If the zero-rating/export refund is not supported by the required documentation, or if payment is not received within the 180-day repatriation period, the claimed zero-rating will be reversed, the output VAT will be clawed back with daily late payment surcharge, and an administrative fine of at least 50% and up to 5 times the tax evaded or falsely refunded may be imposed under the PRC Law on Administration of Tax Collection. Where false export documents are used intentionally to obtain a refund, the entity and responsible personnel face criminal liability for fraudulent export tax refund under the PRC Criminal Law, with penalties including imprisonment and, for especially large amounts, up to life imprisonment and confiscation of property.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) for the mainland-resident Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture; Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) governs the separate HKD clearing corridor for the Hong Kong corporate layer.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The CN_JV_LTD is a PRC-resident joint venture and is therefore within PBOC/SAFE foreign exchange administration. The renminbi is convertible on current account items, so export proceeds from tabletop dice sales, logistics fees, royalties and normal trade disbursements may be settled through banks under authentic trade documentation. Capital account items remain restricted: the Hong Kong shareholder's capital contribution must enter through an FDI foreign exchange capital account, be registered with SAFE, and be supported by a capital verification report before deployment. Profit remittances to the Hong Kong parent are permitted as current account transfers only after annual audit, tax payment certificates and board resolutions are presented; remittance is not an automatic right. Export receipts must be repatriated to China and verified against customs declarations. There is no mandatory universal surrender ratio at present, but retention is capped by the SAFE-authorized settlement account ceiling and surplus balances must be converted into renminbi. The HKD leg is fully convertible under HKMA's linked exchange rate regime, but the PRC JV cannot circumvent PRC capital controls by routing through Hong Kong unless the underlying transaction is lawful and reported.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds earned by the JV must be repatriated into its designated Chinese settlement bank within 180 days from the date of export customs declaration unless a deferred-payment extension is filed through the SAFE trade monitoring system. At present no fixed mandatory conversion ratio applies to current-account export receipts; the JV may retain foreign currency in an approved foreign exchange settlement account up to the ceiling set by SAFE based on its verified trade turnover, and any amount above that ceiling must be settled into RMB. All receipts must be matched against customs export records and bank trade verification filings.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account and RMB Basic Deposit Operational Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB Basic Deposit Account and Current Account Foreign Exchange Settlement Account
RMB Basic Deposit Account, Export Verification Settlement Account and Cross-Border RMB Settlement Rail
Capital Escrow Account and Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMI platforms such as Wise and Revolut are not permitted to open principal corporate deposit accounts for a PRC-resident joint venture, because China's banking rules require deposit-taking institutions to be licensed by PBOC/CBIRC. The JV must operate its treasury and SAFE reporting through a local tier-1 bank. Fintech rails are only an ancillary gate: licensed third-party payment institutions such as PayPal China may collect Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal merchant proceeds and settle those funds into a Chinese bank account after SAFE reconciliation; they cannot replace the corporate banking relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for the JV's statutory legal representative and the appointed account signatories at the time of opening the basic deposit account and the FDI capital account. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted as a substitute; however, the Hong Kong corporate shareholder may execute powers of attorney and board resolutions before a Hong Kong notary public and PRC consular legalization, and a foreign legal representative may attend via the bank's video interview in limited circumstances, followed by an in-branch signatory visit. Capital escrow accounts still require face-to-face KYC verification with the company seal and updated certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sino-foreign beneficial ownership trail loops through a Hong Kong parent, creating layering risk and uncertainty over ultimate controllers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Hong Kong Certificate of Incorporation, Business Registration Certificate, registered office address, annual return, beneficial ownership register maintained under the Hong Kong Companies Ordinance, the JV contract, articles of association, the foreign investment approval certificate, a board resolution approving account opening, bank reference letters for the HK parent, and a source of wealth and source of funds file for each controlling shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FDI capital injection from Hong Kong to the PRC subsidiary may be challenged as unverified or fungible funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE FDI business registration receipt with the Foreign Exchange Registration QR code, capital verification report issued by a PRC certified public accountant, sworn copy of the SWIFT MT103 credit instruction identifying the HK funding bank, bank statements for the HK parent covering the six months prior to transfer, and an explanation of the transaction chain connecting the commercial substance of the joint venture to the injected capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crowdfunding receipts from Kickstarter via Stripe and PayPal resemble advance deposits from anonymous backers, creating refund, sanctions and trade mismatch concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kickstarter campaign agreement, Stripe merchant agreement, PayPal merchant agreement, platform settlement and dispute ledgers, order-level backer and payment records, campaign fulfillment and shipping schedules, production purchase orders, and a revenue recognition memo explaining how pre-sale deposits are converted into export trade proceeds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value exports of epoxy resin RPG dice to diverse end-consignees can be misused for trade-based money laundering or customs misdeclaration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: China customs export declarations, HS code 9504.90 / ISIC 3240 classification memo, commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading and air waybills, carrier delivery confirmations showing weight-to-quantity consistency, epoxy resin supplier certificates and safety data sheets, and completed OFAC/EU/UN/PRC sanctions screening logs for all crowdfunding backers and foreign distributors.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Hong Kong shareholder must complete SAFE FDI registration before wiring. The injection will be routed as a SWIFT MT103 from the HK parent account to the JV's FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account at a designated Chinese tier-1 bank, quoting the SAFE FDI registration number and the Purpose Code for foreign direct investment capital contribution as prescribed by the SAFE/BOP transaction reporting system. Upon receipt, the bank will perform trade verification, and an independent PRC accounting firm will issue the capital verification report. The JV may convert the foreign currency into RMB only for lawful operative purposes and may not use the capital account funds to repay domestic loans or invest in custody wealth management products outside permitted scopes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade payments for epoxy resin, molds, packaging, freight and professional services will be cleared through SWIFT MT103 against documentary evidence such as invoices and contracts. For larger raw material purchases, the JV may issue an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit opened by its Chinese bank in favor of the supplier, with the HK layer acting as a confirming bank when beneficial. Documentary Collections in the form of D/P or D/A will be used for wholesale export receivables and for selective supplier terms. Merchant proceeds from Kickstarter, Stripe and PayPal are settled as pooled foreign currency receipts by licensed payment institutions into the JV's current-account foreign exchange settlement account, with each payout reconciled to the platform settlement report and SAFE trade records. Cross-border RMB payments between the JV and HK counterparties can clear through CIPS in addition to SWIFT messages.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB/USD FX forward contracts with real current-account trade exposure and bank-approved underlying contracts
Onshore foreign exchange swaps and cross-currency swaps for matching HKD/USD working capital flows between the PRC JV and the HK parent company

Offshore RMB non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only in the HK corporate layer's treasury book, not for the PRC JV, since onshore NDF contracts are prohibited without an actual underlying trade transaction
Currency options are permitted on a covered basis for hedging committed export receivables and import payables only

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after each anniversary of the company's date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fees are charged by the period of default: more than 42 days but not more than 3 months, HKD 1,200 (USD 153.85); more than 3 months but not more than 6 months, HKD 2,400 (USD 307.69); more than 6 months but not more than 9 months, HKD 3,600 (USD 461.54); more than 9 months, HKD 4,800 (USD 615.38). The company and every responsible officer may also be prosecuted; upon conviction the maximum penalty is HKD 50,000 (USD 6,410.26) plus a continuing default daily fine of HKD 1,000 (USD 128.21). Prolonged default in filing the Annual Return is an administrative ground for the Companies Registry to strike the company off the register after inquiry, warning, and Gazette publication procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (Form BIR51) together with audited financial statements, auditor's report, and tax computation schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the date of issue of the Profits Tax Return, unless the Inland Revenue Department has approved a filing extension; for a company with a 31 December accounting year end, the IRD commonly permits filing extensions to 15 August for paper/accelerated submissions and later dates for electronic filing where a tax representative has been engaged.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file without reasonable excuse exposes the company to a penalty of HKD 10,000 (USD 1,282.05) and an additional penalty of up to three times the amount of tax undercharged. The Inland Revenue Department may raise a best-of-judgment assessment under section 59(3) of the Inland Revenue Ordinance. Continuing default can result in prosecution, court-imposed fines, elevated assessments, and, where the company remains in serious non-compliance, administrative strike-off may be pursued by the Companies Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, on or before the expiry date stated on the current Business Registration Certificate; a grace period of one month after expiry is available before late renewal surcharges accrue.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late renewal surcharge of HKD 300 (USD 38.46) per month or part of a month applies after the one-month grace period, subject to the statutory cap of HKD 3,000 (USD 384.62). Carrying on business without a valid Business Registration Certificate is an offence; upon conviction the company and responsible officers are liable to a fine of HKD 5,000 (USD 641.03) and one year imprisonment. If the certificate remains unrenewed for a prolonged period, the registration may be cancelled and the company may ultimately be struck off by the Companies Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual verification, audit, and confirmation of statutory registers and the Significant Controllers Register (SCR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No separate filing is required; the registers must be physically available at the Hong Kong registered office or at the place prescribed by law for inspection by the Companies Registry, Inland Revenue Department, and other prescribed law enforcement authorities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous obligation; the SCR must be updated within 7 days after any change in a significant controller, and the Register of Members, Register of Directors and Chief Executives, Register of Company Secretaries, charges records, and minute books must be current at all times. Annual confirmation is reported through the NAR1 Annual Return and through the statutory auditor's review of the registers during the annual audit.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to keep, make available, or update the Significant Controllers Register is a criminal offence; upon conviction a fine of HKD 25,000 (USD 3,205.13) may be imposed, with a further daily default fine of HKD 700 (USD 89.74). Non-compliance with other statutory register and minute book requirements under the Companies Ordinance attracts fines at Level 3 (HKD 10,000 / USD 1,282.05) and continuing daily fines. Material register defects will be reported in the auditor's management letter and are disqualifying to a clean unmodified audit opinion.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Hong Kong Companies Ordinance (Cap.622), every Hong Kong private company limited by shares is required to prepare financial statements that give a true and fair view and to appoint a certified public accountant or certified public accountant firm to audit those financial statements. Hong Kong does not apply turnover, balance-sheet, or headcount exemption thresholds for private companies; mandatory audit is the default rule for all active private companies. The only statutory exception is a dormant private company under Cap.622 section 5 that has not entered into any accounting transactions during the relevant financial period and has delivered the appropriate dormant declaration. For active trading, manufacturing, or e-commerce companies such as the tabletop dice business, a fully qualified independent statutory audit is compulsory in every financial year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants, which are fully aligned with IFRS Accounting Standards. Eligible private entities that are not publicly accountable and that are not required to produce consolidated full-HKFRS statements may apply the Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standard for Private Entities (HKFRS-PE). Tax computations submitted to the Inland Revenue Department must nevertheless be prepared on a basis consistent with the Inland Revenue Ordinance.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not operate a separate 30-day UBO filing window. The statutory mechanism is the Significant Controllers Register (SCR), which requires the company to identify every significant controller, including any individual or entity holding more than 25% of the issued shares or capital, controlling more than 25% of voting rights, or otherwise exercising significant control over the company. The SCR must be updated within 7 days after any change in significant controller particulars, and the company must note the dates of becoming and ceasing to be a significant controller. Share transfers are recorded in the Register of Members as soon as the board accepts the transfer documents, and the cumulative shareholder position is reported annually through Form NAR1, which is due within 42 days after each incorporation anniversary. A 30-day internal register confirmation protocol may be adopted as a governance best practice, but it does not replace the statutory 7-day SCR update rule or the 42-day NAR1 filing deadline.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Chief Executives
Register of Charges and copies of instruments creating charges
Minute Book containing resolutions and proceedings of members and directors
Accounting records and underlying business vouchers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - 1,200 per year (approximately HKD 2,000 - 9,400), covering registered office address, correspondence handling, and the statutory company secretary service.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - 4,500 per year (approximately HKD 12,000 - 35,000) for a small non-listed Hong Kong private company with straightforward manufacturing/trading transactions, inventory, and payment rails, exclusive of ad hoc restructuring or group consolidation work.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: China provides a 15% reduced Corporate Income Tax (CIT) rate for certified High and New Technology Enterprises, a 15% rate for qualifying encouraged industries in the Hainan Free Trade Port and Western Regions, a 100% additional deduction for qualifying R&D expenditures (total 200% deduction of eligible R&D expenses), and preferential small-and-low-profit enterprise rates for taxpayers satisfying the statutory thresholds. No general patent box regime applies, and statutory tax holidays are limited to specific encouraged sectors and regional incentive programs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return (Form A) for Resident Enterprises, together with its supporting schedules, filed through the State Taxation Administration's Online Tax Service/e-Tax Platform (portal: etax.chinatax.gov.cn).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return plus quarterly provisional tax filings.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within five months after the end of the fiscal year (for a calendar-year taxpayer, by 31 May). Quarterly provisional payments, when applicable, must be paid and provisionally reported within fifteen days after the end of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification panel: legal name, tax identification number, registered address, industry code, entity classification, incorporation date, and non-resident shareholder ownership schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose every non-resident shareholder, including the Hong Kong parent, on the tax registration and the beneficial ownership schedule. The non-resident shareholding percentage and the last change of ownership must be current and consistent with the certificate of incorporation and shareholder register. If DTA relief is later claimed on dividends, the claim will be denied unless the beneficial owner identity and ownership percentage match this panel. Failure to disclose non-resident ownership is a compliance violation and may attract penalties under the Tax Collection Administration Law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue determination: total operating revenue from sales of handmade sharp-edge epoxy resin liquid-core polyhedral dice, including payments received through Kickstarter, Stripe, PayPal, direct e-commerce, trade fairs, and shipping surcharges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident enterprise obligations are not reduced by the foreign origin of customers. Because the China joint venture is a resident enterprise, its worldwide income is taxable in China. Convert all foreign currency revenue into Renminbi using the central parity rate or the prescribed average exchange rate for the relevant tax period. Do not net out Stripe, PayPal, or Kickstarter processing fees for revenue recognition; those fees are deductible expenses only when properly invoiced and evidenced. Omitting online platform deposits or crediting sales to the Hong Kong parent without a legally effective agency arrangement will be treated as fraudulent understatement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs and expenses: raw materials, epoxy resin, pigment, molds, labor, packaging, logistics, selling and distribution expenses, administrative expenses, and financial expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All related-party purchases, management fees, royalties, or service payments to the Hong Kong parent or other non-resident affiliates must be separately disclosed on the related-party transaction schedule and supported by written contracts, actual service evidence, invoices, receipts, and economic substance proof. A China joint venture may deduct only arm's length amounts for services and intangibles actually rendered in the relevant period; vague cost-sharing, bundled management charges, or payments for IP not used in China must be reversed. Retain original VAT special invoices and customs declarations for imported inputs. Non-resident-related service fees paid without withholding tax treatment will be disallowed and may trigger withholding penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from accounting profit to taxable profit: adjustments for permanent differences, temporary differences, prohibited deductions, transfer pricing adjustments, thin capitalization, and carryforward loss set-off.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report upward adjustments for excessive interest paid to Hong Kong affiliates; for non-financial enterprises the related-party debt-to-equity safe harbor is 2:1, and the disallowed interest portion is not deductible. Loss carryforwards are limited to five years and may not be offset against profits of the Hong Kong parent. When the China JV records a transfer pricing adjustment from a tax audit, reflect the audit adjustment in this reconciliation and maintain the contemporaneous supporting documentation. Non-resident loss pooling or profit shifting through expenditures paid to offshore entities is not permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base and tax computation: taxable income, applicable tax rate, calculated CIT before credits, reduced tax, exempt tax, tax credits, and tax due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the statutory 25% headline rate unless an approved 15% High and New Technology Enterprise rate applies. If the JV claims preferential incentives, attach the applicable qualification certificate and contemporaneous records. This box must also feed the calculation of the withholding tax on the profits distributed to non-resident shareholders: the JV, as the distributing resident enterprise, is the withholding agent for non-resident enterprise income tax. Reinstating prior tax holidays without eligibility documents is a red flag; the tax authority will assess under-claimed tax with interest and penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits and prepayments: foreign tax credit, direct and indirect foreign tax credits, tax credit carryovers, quarterly provisional payments already made, final tax due, and refund claim.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all foreign taxes paid on overseas-derived income and attach supporting schedules. Quarterly provisional payments must be credited against the final annual liability. For a distribution to the Hong Kong parent, compute statutory withholding tax on the declared dividend; if treaty relief is claimed, include the reduced 5% rate only where the Hong Kong beneficial owner meets the 25% direct-holding requirement and submits the applicable Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership statement. This box should reconcile the exact amount of non-resident withholding tax to be reported on the separate non-resident withholding return before the outbound remittance occurs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident payment and withholding reconciliation schedule: outbound dividend, interest, and royalty payments, contract registration numbers, tax clearance certificates, and withholding tax deposits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File the contract registration with the required tax authority before payment execution, or obtain the electronic contract registration number, as applicable, and submit the non-resident enterprise withholding return with the actual withholding tax payment. Remittance abroad without the withholding tax payment or tax clearance certificate is a fatal error for the China-HK cross-border structure. If the Hong Kong parent fails to provide the annual Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership declaration, apply the domestic statutory 10% rate and later apply for a refund only as permitted by treaty mechanics. Keep all DTA claim files for at least ten years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under the Law of the People's Republic of China on Tax Collection and Administration (TCAA), late filing attracts a fine of up to CNY 2,000 for ordinary cases or CNY 2,000 to CNY 10,000 for serious cases; under-declaration by deception attracts a fine of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax and a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% for overdue tax. Failure to withhold non-resident enterprise income tax may attract a penalty of 50% to 300% of the amount not withheld under TCAA Article 69. False returns with tax evaded exceeding CNY 100,000 and exceeding 10% of the payable tax may trigger criminal proceedings under Article 201 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, with imprisonment of up to seven years and fines for the responsible persons.
